newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: BP chief urges Colombia to stay competitive.
newsitem.headline: BP chief urges Colombia to stay competitive.

text.p: The head of British Petroleum Co Plc's worldwide operations, John Browne, called on Colombia to keep the terms of investment in its oil industry competitive during a visit on Monday.

BP is the biggest single foreign investor in Colombia but has consistently said the terms of its association contract with state oil company Ecopetrol to exploit the promising Piedemonte field are not profitable enough.

The British oil multinational is currently involved in protracted negotiations to revise the contract and hopes the outcome will provide wider profit margins and a platform for long-term involvement in Colombia.
"I believe exploitation and production has a very strong future in Colombia but the future is always very competitive," Browne said after a closed doors meeting with President Ernesto Samper.

"Across the world people are always finding new things to do so its important for Colombia to make sure that what's done to attract ... foreign companies is kept attractive compared to the rest of the world."
Browne recognised the ever-present threat of attacks against oil infrastructure by leftist guerrillas was a constant worry in Colombia but praised the effectiveness of the army.
